events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.69 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered ride, so route deviation mileage enters the fare directly [F6][RD-2]. No traffic incident qualifies under RD-4(a): F14 records none, and the speed-band facts (F11–F13) are only corroborative and cannot exempt a segment on their own [F11][F14][RD-4].

Segment F3 (22:58–23:05, 3.82 km driven vs 1.91 km optimal, +1.91 km, up to 780 m off the optimal route) is the off-route stretch [F3][RD-1]. The only rider messages before 22:58:50 are F7 and F8, which are a pickup-arrangement exchange and contain no agreement to any route at all [F7][F8]. The driver's account that he went round Central Expressway because it was crawling appears only in his post-trip statement [F10]; a driver's own statement that the rider agreed, or his own reason for the diversion, is not rider consent [F10][RD-5]. The chat record is complete and timestamped with no rider agreement before the segment, so the finding is "counts", ground consent_after_or_none [F7][F8][F9][RD-5].

No RD-3 stop applies: F3 measures a driven segment, not a stop the rider named, and no rider message names any place other than the pickup kerb [F3][F7][RD-3]. RD-6 is not triggered because the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so no account flag arises [F17][RD-6].

Amount: the unexempt segment's extra distance is 1.91 km [F3]; the trip rate is $18.60 ÷ 13.19 km = $1.4102/km [F6][F4], giving 1.91 km × $1.4102/km = $2.6935 → $2.69. The trace's allowed formula uses $1.4102/km on the segment extra_km, and F3 is the segment the trace feeds to the formula; the separate excess figure in F4 covers all extra mileage and is not the segment figure. Refund is $2.69, issued as a voucher per NS-7 [RD-2][NS-7].
